Hi Irene,

Quick intro — we (BrightPath) are finalizing the AV stack for the May 12 hybrid event and want to check the encoder certification steps you require for ON24/Zoom capture. Two items in particular:

1) Encoder codec/profile — we currently run the stream with H.264, 6Mbps, keyframe 2s. Is there a minimum profile for Redwood/ON24 ingest to preserve real-time captions and recording sync?

2) Registrant tokenization — our registration system can append an encrypted token as a URL param for each registrant (for sponsor analytics and replay gating). Does Redwood require a specific token format (TTL, signed payload) or is a simple UUID sufficient? If you have a spec we can align to, that’d save integration time.

We can do a short technical call this week; Owen from ON24 is copied in.

Thanks — Samira

Hi Samira — thanks for the details. Short answers up front, longer notes below:

- Codec/profile: H.264 @ 6Mbps is fine for capture, but we recommend baseline/main profile with CABAC turned on off for low-latency modes; keyframe 1–2s is acceptable. We'll need encoder config to run a quick ingest test.
- Token format: we prefer a signed JWT with a short TTL (recommended 24 hours for live access, longer for replay if gating is required). UUID-only tokens are OK for basic analytics but won’t allow us to validate replay entitlement.

I’ve attached a registrant-token spec and an encoder config template for your AV team to use. Ben, can you confirm the ingest test window and what artifacts you want back (packet logs, wav extract, sample MP4)?

Proposed next steps:
- BrightPath to push live test stream to our staging endpoint Monday 4/5 09:00–10:00 PT.
- Redwood to run capture + produce a 60s trimmed clip and provide packet/latency metrics.
- If token signing is required, Samira to confirm whether BrightPath will sign tokens or if Redwood should issue signed tokens at registration time (tradeoffs below).

If that schedule works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Hi all — technical quick win checklist from infra/ops perspective:

1) Staging ingest endpoint: rwinf-staging-ingest.redwood.com:1935 (RTMP + SRT supported). Please confirm which protocol BrightPath will use; SRT preferred for packet recovery.
2) Encoder config: attached is encoder_config_v3.yaml (uses baseline/main H264, 1080p30, 6–8Mbps). Please make sure low-latency mode is off if you want reliable captions.
3) Logging artifacts: we’ll collect ffmpeg logs, a 60s trimmed MP4, and RTP/SRT packet capture (pcap). We will also extract an audio WAV for caption sync checks.
4) Token validation: if BrightPath signs JWTs, we need the public key (PEM) ahead of the test. If Redwood is issuing tokens, we’ll need a webhook from your registration system so we can mint an access token and return the shareable URL.

Proposed test schedule: 2027-04-05 09:00–09:30 PT — warm up + steady-state; 09:30–09:45 PT — 60s capture for QA artifacts. Ben and one infra engineer (remote) will be on the call.

Thanks — quick product/ops notes:

- Sponsor tracking: BrightPath wants per-registrant sponsor attribution to display in replay analytics. That means the token payload must include sponsor_id and registrant_id (or a pointer we can dereference). Prefer signed JWT so we can trust payload.
- Privacy: ensure tokens don’t carry PII (no emails in the JWT). If BrightPath needs email-level gating, use a short lived token + separate auth call to pull entitlement.
- Access: for replay gating we’ll need the token TTL to be configurable; recommend 90 days for sponsor replay access by default.

Samira — confirm whether you can produce signed JWTs or want Redwood to mint tokens on registration webhook. If BrightPath handles signing, we’ll need the PEM and a test token before 4/5.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Events Program Manager — Redwood Inference
